plain: Offense or resentment, as in taking umbrage at a remark

webster.text: A shade; a skreen of trees; as the umbrage of woods.

example.quote: He objected to proceeding to change the Government without the approbation of Congress, as being improper and giving just umbrage to that body.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, September 10, 1787
